architecture_decisions.decision: ONE new leaf crate `fe-canonical-log` (new root Cargo.toml workspace member) hosts ALL pure canonical-log logic: deterministic CBOR codec, envelope grammar, signing/op_id/AAD, nano-unit bridge, author-key lifecycle, capability certificate chains, branch/frontier/checkpoint, quarantine/retention, segment/shard artifacts, the SPEC-7 wire types, and the SPEC-4 identity/trait layer. It depends DOWN only on fe-sdk (nano-unit newtypes) plus leaf externals (blake3, ed25519-dalek, multibase, unicode-normalization, thiserror, serde, data-encoding, zeroize, rand, and — pending approval — chacha20poly1305/x25519-dalek). It must never depend on fe-runtime (pulls bevy+tokio, confirmed at fe-runtime/Cargo.toml:11-13), fe-identity (bevy+iroh+keyring), fe-policy, fe-database, or surrealdb.
architecture_decisions.rationale: The eight per-spec contracts independently proposed five different crate names (fe-oplog, fe-canonical-log, fe-canon-log, fe-capability, fe-canonical-wire), each with its own canonical-CBOR implementation. Two canonical encoders in one workspace is a byte-divergence bug factory: SPEC-7 §4.1 requires its re-encode of a complete envelope to be byte-identical to SPEC-1's encoder, and SPEC-3/5/6 all reuse the SPEC-1 CBOR profile. A single leaf crate gives one encoder, one Scope/Hash32/Identifier32/Hlc/Author/SortedFrontier vocabulary, and a diamond (fe-database, fe-api, fe-sync all depend on it) with no cycle.
architecture_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Five separate crates as proposed (duplicate codecs, five sets of primitive types needing mechanical reconciliation); putting the codec in fe-database (fe-api/fe-sync would then need fe-database for wire types); putting capability certs in fe-policy (see cycle decision); reusing fe-format's canonical-JSON Ed25519 signer (explicitly forbidden — manifests only, wrong encoding, wrong id derivation).

architecture_decisions.decision: Hand-roll the deterministic CBOR codec in fe-canonical-log/src/cbor.rs. Do NOT add ciborium (or minicbor/serde_cbor).
architecture_decisions.rationale: ciborium 0.2.2 is already in Cargo.lock transitively, but its serde-derived output is NOT the RFC 8949 §4.2.1 profile SPEC-1 §2 mandates: it does not guarantee sorted map keys, does not reject non-minimal integer arguments, indefinite lengths, floats, tags, or non-NFC text on decode. Every contract that proposed ciborium also proposed a hand-written canonicalization layer on top — at which point the crate buys nothing but a dependency and a second place for byte drift. The golden vectors (docs/spec/canonical-log/operation-envelope-v1.json, 4 vectors) demand byte-exact encode AND strict reject-on-decode, which is ~400 lines of explicit code.
architecture_decisions.alternatives_rejected: ciborium + a canonicalization pass (still needs the strict decoder; adds a dep whose default behavior a future edit could accidentally rely on); ciborium::Value as the internal value model (its Float/Tag variants are unrepresentable states the spec forbids).

architecture_decisions.decision: i64 nano-unit newtypes (Nanometers, Nanodegrees, ScalePartsPerBillion, NanoVec3) live in fe-sdk/src/units.rs; fe-canonical-log depends down on fe-sdk for them. fe-sdk gains ZERO crypto/CBOR dependencies, and the CBOR bridge (units_codec.rs) lives on the fe-canonical-log side.
architecture_decisions.rationale: D-CL5 mandates plugin-facing exposure via fe-sdk typed newtypes, and fe-sdk is already the base of the graph (fe-runtime/Cargo.toml:21 depends on it; fe-terrain, fe-plugin, fe-plugin-test, fe-ui also consume it directly). A one-directional fe-canonical-log -> fe-sdk edge can never invert. Adding a NEW module (not changing PropertyValue/PrimitiveDescriptor) keeps the change strictly additive, so fe-terrain (a forbidden file tree) keeps compiling unmodified.
architecture_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Defining the newtypes in fe-canonical-log (would force fe-sdk -> fe-canonical-log for plugin exposure, i.e. crypto deps in the WASM-facing stable API); adding a PropertyValue::NanoScalar variant now (PropertyValue is not #[non_exhaustive]; a new variant breaks exhaustive matches in fe-terrain/fe-ui, both locked).

architecture_decisions.decision: Capability certificate chains, verification, delegation/attenuation, and scope-epoch types live in fe-canonical-log/src/capability/. fe-policy is not modified at all and stays crypto-free; fe-canonical-log defines its own SPEC-1-native Scope map and does not import fe_policy::Scope.
architecture_decisions.rationale: SPEC-3 §2.1 requires certs on the same canonical binary encoding as envelopes (no JSON/JWT in the trust domain), so cert code must sit next to the CBOR/BLAKE3/Ed25519 machinery. Putting it in fe-policy would (a) risk a fe-policy -> fe-canonical-log -> fe-policy cycle the moment the codec needed Scope/RoleLevel, and (b) push chacha20poly1305/x25519-dalek/blake3 into all six fe-policy consumers, two of which (fe-webview, fe-plugin) currently pull no crypto through it. fe-policy::Scope is a display string; SPEC-1 §3.1's scope map is binary Identifier32 — conflating them would corrupt the wire form.
architecture_decisions.alternatives_rejected: fe-policy/src/capability.rs as SPEC-3's contract proposed (cycle + dependency blast radius); a dedicated fe-capability crate (duplicate CBOR codec again).

architecture_decisions.decision: ALL SurrealDB persistence for the canonical path lives in fe-database: fe-database/src/canon_log/ (verified_op_log, materializer_apply_marker, scope_epoch_state, branch/checkpoint/quarantine/lease rows, admission, replay, rebuild) and fe-database/src/migration/ (SPEC-8). fe-canonical-log declares storage seams as traits only and has no surrealdb dependency.
architecture_decisions.rationale: fe-database is the only crate holding `Db`, `Repo`, `define_table!`, the HLC allocator and the log-first seam (fe-database/src/op_log.rs:93). Keeping the leaf crate I/O-free is what lets every SPEC-2/3/5/6 module be unit-tested with in-memory fakes and keeps fe-api/fe-sync from inheriting an embedded database through a types crate.
architecture_decisions.alternatives_rejected: SPEC-5's contract proposal to put self-contained SurrealDB adapters (with hand-written DDL) inside the canonical-log crate — that duplicates schema authority, pulls surrealdb into a leaf, and creates two places that define canonical tables.

architecture_decisions.decision: fe-canonical-log carries its own minimal did:key codec (multibase base58btc + 0xed01 multicodec) rather than depending on fe-identity, with a byte-compatibility test against the exact fixture DID in operation-envelope-v1.json.
architecture_decisions.rationale: SPEC-1 §3.2 requires the Author map's DID<->public_key binding check at envelope-verify time, inside the codec. fe-identity/src/did_key.rs already implements the identical algorithm but the crate drags bevy, iroh, keyring and jsonwebtoken, which is unacceptable weight for a codec used by every consumer. multibase 0.9 is already a direct dependency of fe-identity (fe-identity/Cargo.toml:23) so this adds no new supply-chain surface.
architecture_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Depending on fe-identity (heavy, and would make fe-sync/fe-api pull the codec's crypto through an identity crate); extracting a shared fe-did crate (a fourth new crate for ~40 lines).

architecture_decisions.decision: SPEC-8 dual-emit is a RUNTIME mode enum parsed from the local process env var FE_MIGRATION_MODE (legacy_only default; seam_ready, dual_emit_shadow, shadow_rebuild reachable; canonical_authoritative_local defined but hard-refused by the parser). Not a cargo feature, not a database or config row.
architecture_decisions.rationale: SPEC-8 §2.2 requires the flag to be local-only (never arriving from a network, peer message, or replicated row) and requires the process to state its mode in diagnostics — both point at a runtime value, not a compile-time feature. A cargo feature also cannot be default-off per process and would force a rebuild to change, breaking the 'legacy editor keeps working, canonical lands alongside' constraint. A DB row would be replicable, i.e. exactly the vector §2.2 forbids.
architecture_decisions.alternatives_rejected: cargo feature `canonical-dual-emit` (no runtime diagnostics, rebuild required, feature unification could enable it transitively); a SurrealDB settings row (replicable — forbidden); a CLI flag on fractalengine main.rs (would require editing the binary's startup, out of scope this wave).

architecture_decisions.decision: The canonical path reuses fe-database's existing process-global HLC (fe-database/src/op_log.rs:26-82) as its monotonic (wall_ms, counter) source. No per-verse HLC state is introduced.
architecture_decisions.rationale: SPEC-4 §4.3's deterministic replay order is (wall_ms, counter, author.public_key); the author public key breaks any tie a shared counter could produce across verses, so per-verse sequences buy no ordering property. A global monotonic clock is also strictly safer for the equivocation rule in SPEC-1 §6 than N independent counters. init_hlc must already have run before any canonical append — the canonical commit seam asserts this rather than lazily initializing.
architecture_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Per-verse HLC state keyed by verse_id (new persisted state, no ordering benefit, and a partition/restart correctness risk); deriving HLC from wall clock at append time (violates SPEC-4 §4.1's ban on local-clock-derived state).

architecture_decisions.decision: XChaCha20-Poly1305 seal/open and the X25519 HPKE-style scope-key wrap are isolated in fe-canonical-log/src/crypto/ behind AeadSuite/ScopeKeyResolver/ScopeKeyStore traits. SPEC-1's foundation computes only the AAD preimages and the EncryptionParams metadata; it never runs a cipher. suite_id=65535 decodes successfully (the golden-vector oracle requires it) but EncryptionParams::assert_production_suite() errors, and every seal/open and admission path calls it.
architecture_decisions.rationale: chacha20poly1305 and x25519-dalek are the only genuinely new third-party crates in this workstream (confirmed absent from Cargo.lock; iroh's crypto_box vendors chacha20/poly1305/aead/curve25519-dalek transitively but exposes no importable AEAD or X25519 API). Confining them to one module means the foundation, capability, branch, wire and materialize work all compile and test without them, so a dependency-approval delay blocks one slice instead of the workstream. The spec is silent on which layer must reject the fixture suite (SPEC-1 §3.5 vs §7), so pinning it to seal/open + admission is an explicit, testable choice.
architecture_decisions.alternatives_rejected: AEAD inside the codec module (makes the whole foundation depend on unapproved crates); the `hpke` crate for a literal RFC 9180 construction (heavier, unaudited here, and SPEC-3 §10.2 says 'HPKE-style', with its own explicit KDF/AAD/signature construction already specified); rejecting suite_id=65535 at decode time (would fail the golden vectors, which exercise that fixture through decode/encode/signature/op_id).

architecture_decisions.decision: Cross-module composition — implementing SPEC-6's CheckpointView over SPEC-5's SignedCheckpointClaim, SPEC-4's CandidateVerifier over the envelope+capability+author-key stack, segment SealedArtifactStore over a byte store, ScopeKeyResolver over the crypto key store — is deferred to the serial integration wave (fe-canonical-log/src/compose.rs). Parallel leaves define and consume traits only.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Three specs each describe a 'checkpoint' (SPEC-4 CheckpointBinding, SPEC-5 SignedCheckpointClaim, SPEC-6 CheckpointView) and three describe a 'quarantine reason'. If parallel leaves wired concrete types to each other they would either collide on files or freeze each other's APIs mid-flight. Traits in leaves + one serial composition pass is the same leaf/integration split that worked for the Spatial Builder program (Wave 1 leaves, then a serial integration pass).
architecture_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Concrete cross-type coupling inside wave 2 (compile-order coupling between sibling slices with no arbiter); a single mega-slice owning all of fe-canonical-log (no parallelism, one agent holding eight specs).

architecture_decisions.decision: The legacy write path is never edited. Canonical commit is a NEW function (fe-database/src/migration/boundary.rs::commit_operation_dual_emit) that CALLS the existing, unmodified op_log::commit_operation for the legacy half and derives the canonical candidate on a side channel that never writes the live SurrealDB projection. update_node_url_handler's pre-existing op-log bypass and the six D-CL20 multi-row mutations get bypass COUNTERS only, never invented canonical payloads.
architecture_decisions.rationale: HARD CONSTRAINT 2 plus SPEC-8 §2.1: legacy behavior and error semantics must be byte-for-bit unchanged, so wrapping is strictly safer than modifying. SPEC-8 §4.2.5 and D-CL20 forbid inventing canonical schemas for GLTF import, node rename/duplicate, and Verse/Fractal/Petal creation; instrumenting them as permanently unmapped is the compliant outcome and correctly keeps promotion blocked (unmapped_bypass_count > 0 forever, for now).
architecture_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Editing commit_operation to fork internally (changes the live editor's hot path and its error strings); mapping the D-CL20 kinds to make coverage metrics look green (explicitly forbidden); skipping the bypass counters (then SPEC-8 §6.1 Ingress coverage would be unmeasurable rather than measurably blocked).

slices.title: fe-canonical-log crate + deterministic CBOR + envelope grammar + signing/op_id/AAD + nano units + golden vectors
slices.brief: Create the new leaf crate `fe-canonical-log` and add it to the root Cargo.toml [workspace] members list, then implement the entire SPEC-1 foundation that all seven later slices compile against. Implement in fe-canonical-log/src/cbor.rs a hand-written canonical CBOR value model (`CborValue` with Uint/NegInt/Bytes/Text/Array/Map/Null and NOTHING else) plus `encode_canonical`/`decode_canonical`: definite lengths only (reject additional-info 31), shortest-form integer and length arguments (reject non-minimal on decode), reject floats, tags (major 6), undefined and every simple value except 0xf6, reject duplicate map keys, reject map keys not in strictly ascending order of their own canonical-encoded bytes (plain bytewise RFC 8949 order, NOT length-first), reject trailing bytes, and reject any decoded text string that differs from its own NFC normalization (use unicode-normalization; the oracle's assertNfc checks every string in the tree, which is broader than the prose of §2.5 — match the oracle). Implement fe-canonical-log/src/did_key.rs as a self-contained did:key codec (multibase base58btc 'z', multicodec prefix [0xed,0x01], exactly 32 bytes) mirroring the algorithm in fe-identity/src/did_key.rs without depending on fe-identity, using the `multibase = "0.9"` crate already used at fe-identity/Cargo.toml:23. Implement fe-canonical-log/src/envelope.rs with Hash32, Identifier32, Scope (verse_id + Option<petal_id> + Option<resource_id>, plus `contains(&self, child) -> bool` implementing SPEC-3 §1.7 containment: a non-null parent petal/resource must match exactly, a null parent field may be narrowed by the child but a non-null one may never be widened), Author (did + public_key), CapabilityRef (chain_id + scope_epoch), Hlc (wall_ms + counter), EncryptionParams (suite_id + key_id + 24-byte nonce, with `is_fixture_only_suite()` and `assert_production_suite()`), PayloadEncryption, PayloadRef (with `empty()` = BLAKE3(no bytes) + length 0 + None), UnsignedEnvelope (keys 0..9) and CompleteEnvelope (keys 0..10), each with to_cbor/from_cbor/encode_canonical/decode_canonical enforcing exactly the listed integer keys once each, protocol_version == 1, non-zero operation_kind, resource_id requiring a non-null petal_id, the no-payload form requiring length 0 and BLAKE3(empty), and strictly ascending unique parents. Implement fe-canonical-log/src/frontier.rs with `SortedFrontier` (strictly sorted, deduplicated, non-empty Vec<Hash32> with `try_new`, `as_slice`, and `commitment() -> Hash32` = BLAKE3 over the concatenated 32-byte op_ids in lexicographic order) — this is the single D-CL19 frontier primitive that SPEC-4, SPEC-5, SPEC-6 and SPEC-7 all reuse, so nothing downstream may define its own. Implement fe-canonical-log/src/signing.rs with `SIGNATURE_DOMAIN = b"fe-oplog-v1\0"`, `signature_preimage`, `sign_envelope`, `verify_envelope` (which first re-derives the Ed25519 key from author.did and rejects any mismatch against author.public_key before verifying), `op_id` = BLAKE3 of the COMPLETE envelope bytes including the 64-byte signature at key 10, plus generic `sign_domain(key, domain, body)` / `verify_domain(key, domain, body, sig)` helpers (ASCII domain || 0x00 || body) that every later slice reuses for its own artifact domain. Implement fe-canonical-log/src/payload_aad.rs with `PAYLOAD_AAD_DOMAIN = b"fe-oplog-payload-aad-v1\0"`, `payload_aad_envelope_cbor` (keys 0..8 verbatim plus a trimmed key-9 map containing only the encryption submap) and `payload_aad_preimage`, both erroring when payload.encryption is None. Implement fe-canonical-log/src/kind.rs with OperationKind (NormalIntent=1, BranchGenesis=2, DetachedMerge=3, ScopeEpochBump=4, Application(u16) for 5..=65535) and `validate_structural_rules` covering everything §6 derives from ONE envelope: kind 2 has zero parents, kind 1 has >=1 parent and an Encrypted payload, kind 3 has >=2 parents, kind 4 has exactly one parent and the no-payload form; kinds >=5 pass through structurally unvalidated (no schema registry exists — leave a pointer comment). Add fe-sdk/src/units.rs with Nanometers, Nanodegrees, ScalePartsPerBillion and NanoVec3 (all i64, Debug/Clone/Copy/PartialEq/Eq/Serialize/Deserialize, From<i64>, NanoVec3::new/as_array) and export them from fe-sdk/src/lib.rs — this is a purely ADDITIVE change: do not touch PropertyValue, PrimitiveDescriptor, or any existing fe-sdk type, because fe-terrain and fe-ui match on those exhaustively and are locked files. Add fe-canonical-log/src/units_codec.rs bridging NanoVec3 to a 3-element canonical CBOR signed-integer array (full i64::MIN..=i64::MAX range). Write fe-canonical-log/Cargo.toml declaring the COMPLETE dependency set every later slice needs so no later slice edits it: serde, serde_json, thiserror, blake3, ed25519-dalek (all workspace = true), multibase = "0.9", unicode-normalization = "0.1", data-encoding = "2", zeroize = "1", rand = "0.8", async-trait = "0.1", ulid (workspace), fe-sdk = { path = "../fe-sdk" }, chacha20poly1305 = "0.10" and x25519-dalek = "2" (the last two are pending owner dependency approval — declare them and note it in AGENTS.md), and dev-dependencies hex = "0.4" plus tokio (workspace, for wire tests). Write fe-canonical-log/src/lib.rs declaring the full module tree — cbor, did_key, envelope, frontier, signing, payload_aad, kind, units_codec, capability, author_key, branch, checkpoint, retention, segment, wire, materialize, crypto, compose — and create EMPTY placeholder files (a single doc comment, no submodule declarations, no code) for capability/mod.rs, author_key/mod.rs, branch/mod.rs, checkpoint.rs, retention/mod.rs, segment/mod.rs, wire/mod.rs, materialize/mod.rs, crypto/mod.rs and compose.rs so that later slices own their own subtrees and NEVER edit lib.rs. Write fe-canonical-log/src/AGENTS.md recording: why the codec is hand-rolled rather than ciborium, why the crate must never depend on fe-runtime/fe-identity/fe-policy/surrealdb, the dependency-direction rule (fe-canonical-log -> fe-sdk only, never the reverse), and the module ownership map. Write fe-canonical-log/tests/golden_vectors.rs reproducing all six §7 conformance points for all four vectors in docs/spec/canonical-log/operation-envelope-v1.json, plus a test asserting assert_production_suite() errors on the suite_id=65535 fixture while decode/encode/signature/op_id still succeed for it. Add colocated #[cfg(test)] modules per file per repo style (terse one-line doc comments in code, rationale in AGENTS.md). You MUST NOT edit any file under fe-ui/ or fe-terrain/, must not touch fe-database, fe-api, fe-sync or fe-identity, and must not run cargo build/test/clippy — the orchestrator runs one serial gate.
slices.acceptance: cargo check --workspace --tests, cargo test --workspace and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings all pass; `cargo test -p fe-canonical-log --test golden_vectors` reproduces all four operation-envelope-v1.json vectors byte-exactly (unsigned round-trip, signature verify, complete round-trip + reconstruct, op_id, ciphertext_hash, payload plaintext + AAD preimage) and the suite_id=65535 fixture-rejection test passes; `node --test docs/spec/canonical-log/operation-envelope-v1.test.mjs` still passes; git diff --name-only shows no fe-ui/** or fe-terrain/** change; fe-sdk/Cargo.toml is unchanged (no new deps in fe-sdk).

slices.title: SPEC-3 capability certificates, chain verification, permission table, blinded topic labels
slices.brief: Implement the SPEC-3 capability trust domain inside fe-canonical-log/src/capability/, importing every shared primitive from the wave-1 foundation and defining none of your own: use fe_canonical_log::envelope::{Hash32, Identifier32, Scope, Author as Principal, CapabilityRef}, fe_canonical_log::cbor::{CborValue, encode_canonical, decode_canonical}, fe_canonical_log::signing::{sign_domain, verify_domain}, fe_canonical_log::did_key::parse_did_key, and Scope::contains for §1.7 containment. Read docs/spec/canonical-log/capabilities-and-revocation.md §1, §2.1 encoding rules, §2.2 the fifteen-key certificate grammar, §2.3 the six-key caveat map, §2.4 the chain grammar and its nine numbered verification steps, §3.1 verb bits, §3.2 object-class bits, §3.3 the effective permission table, §4 delegation and attenuation, §5.1 the scope_epoch_bump operation shape, §5.3 the revalidation/caching contract, and §6.1 the blinded topic label derivation. Produce: certificate.rs (Certificate with all 15 fields, encode_unsigned over keys 0..13, signature preimage ASCII"fe-capability-cert-v1"||0x00||unsigned, sign/verify_signature, certificate_id = BLAKE3 of the complete cert, rejection of unknown caveat keys, rejection of empty verb/object-class bitsets, and strict-ascending-no-duplicate validation of allowed_schema_hashes/resource_allowlist/allowed_operation_kinds); verbs.rs (VerbSet and ObjectClassSet bitsets with the exact 0x01..0x20 bit values, subset/contains helpers); caveats.rs (Caveats plus `attenuates(&self, child) -> bool` where numeric caveats must satisfy child <= parent, array caveats must satisfy child ⊆ parent including the empty set as a valid maximal narrowing, and a non-null parent caveat may never become null in a child); chain.rs (Chain root-first with leaf_certificate_id, chain_id = BLAKE3 of the complete chain, and `verify_chain(chain, req, snapshot)` executing §2.4 steps 1-9 IN ORDER and short-circuiting with a typed error per step: canonical re-encode round-trip equality, per-cert signature + DID/public-key binding, root has no parent and its issuer is Manager+ per the injected snapshot, parent-link and epoch-family equality (issuer_authority_id/epoch_scope/scope_epoch equal to root, parent_certificate_id[i]==certificate_id[i-1], issuer[i]==audience[i-1]), strict attenuation at every hop, leaf-audience binding (equals req.requester for non-append verbs, equals req.operation_author for append), the not_before/not_after window plus the 24h maximum total lifetime and operation_scope_epoch equality, per-caveat fit of the requested verb/class/scope/resource/size/schema/kind/preview-hz, and finally snapshot epoch equality subject to a caller-supplied causal-replay override); permissions.rs (§3.3 as `fn permitted(verb, class) -> bool` plus the documented extras: append/op additionally requires the operation kind to be in allowed_operation_kinds for a structural op, append/checkpoint additionally requires Manager+); revalidation.rs (§5.3's CacheKey keyed by (chain_id, epoch_scope, epoch, expiry_ms, authority_view_version), PinnedSession::is_still_valid returning Valid | ReauthorizationRequired | Expired, an AuthorizationView trait, and a RevalidationGate with on_epoch_bump invalidation — pure and UNWIRED, no fe-api/fe-network call sites); and topic.rs (§6.1: the five-key topic label map, topic_key = BLAKE3_keyed(scope_key, ASCII"fe-topic-key-v1"||0x00||canonical (scope,epoch) pair), topic_digest = BLAKE3_keyed(topic_key, ASCII"fe-topic-v1"||0x00||canonical label), topic_name = "fe-topic-v1/" + lowercase unpadded RFC 4648 base32 via the data-encoding crate, three lanes separated). AuthorizationSnapshot must be a plain injected struct ({root_issuer_is_manager_plus, current_epoch, epoch_causally_valid_for_op}) — do NOT query a database, do NOT import fe-policy, and do NOT implement SPEC-2's authority history (a later slice supplies the snapshot). Do not perform any AEAD or X25519 work: scope keys arrive as an already-resolved [u8;32] parameter. Write fe-canonical-log/src/capability/AGENTS.md explaining why certs live here rather than in fe-policy (cycle + dependency blast radius) and why the SPEC-1 scope map is deliberately distinct from fe_policy::Scope. Add colocated #[cfg(test)] modules covering the §8 conformance behaviors that need no DB: golden-style chain round-trip against a committed fixture you generate as fe-canonical-log/tests/fixtures/capability-chain-v1.json, non-canonical CBOR rejection, link/signature substitution rejection, nine independent widening attempts each failing with NotAttenuated, TTL/not-before/leaf-binding enforcement, permission-table denials, deterministic and lane-separated topic derivation, and no raw identifier leaking into a topic name. Assert specific typed error variants, never a bare is_err(). You MUST NOT edit fe-canonical-log/src/lib.rs, Cargo.toml, any sibling module directory, fe-database, fe-api, fe-sync, fe-identity, fe-policy, fe-ui/** or fe-terrain/**, and MUST NOT run cargo.
slices.acceptance: Workspace gate green (cargo test --workspace + clippy -D warnings); the committed capability-chain-v1.json fixture round-trips byte-exactly through Certificate/Chain encode+decode with matching certificate_id/chain_id/signatures; every §8 test that does not require durable epoch state exists and asserts a specific typed error variant; no file outside the declared owned_files is modified.

slices.title: SPEC-2 author key rotation, lineage, disavow/rescind, continuity grant, admission
slices.brief: Implement the SPEC-2 author-key lifecycle inside fe-canonical-log/src/author_key/, reusing wave-1 primitives exclusively (fe_canonical_log::envelope::{Hash32, Scope, Author, Hlc}, cbor encode/decode, signing::{sign_domain, verify_domain}, did_key::parse_did_key) and defining no new Scope/Hash/Hlc types. Read docs/spec/canonical-log/author-key-lifecycle.md §2.2-§2.5, §3 and §3.1-§3.5, §4.1-§4.7, §5, §6 and §6.1-§6.5, §7 (conformance cases 1-14) and §9.1-§9.4. Produce payloads.rs with RotationStatement (the nine numeric-keyed fields of §3.1) and RotationPayload (statement + 64-byte successor signature), each with canonical CBOR to/from bytes and a `validate_against_envelope` returning Result that checks every equality rule in the §3.1 table (scope, branch_id, parent op_id, scope_epoch, predecessor DID and public key all byte-equal to the enclosing envelope) — these must be checked at admission against a RECEIVED payload, not merely enforced by construction. Produce rotation_proof.rs implementing the §3.2 successor dual proof with domain b"fe-author-key-rotation-v1\0" over the canonical statement bytes, using verify_domain and ed25519_dalek verify_strict semantics, plus the successor DID<->public-key binding check and the structural successor != predecessor rejection. Produce lineage.rs implementing the §4 active-key state machine as PURE in-memory logic over a caller-supplied `CausalOperationView` trait (parents/is_admitted/reaches): LineageIndex::record_rotation returns Applied or Fork and rejects lineage cycles, duplicate successor transitions, and a predecessor not active at the parent-induced state; active_key_at resolves Active/Retired/ForkedUnresolved/Unknown at a causal point (never by newest-observed or wall clock) and honors §2.5 scope propagation via Scope::contains (a verse-scope rotation applies to descendant petal/resource scopes; a narrower rotation never leaks outside its subtree or across verses). Produce disavow.rs implementing the §6 six-field disavow payload with canonical CBOR, last_hlc >= first_hlc validation, and a DisavowIndex whose matching_disavows/is_disavowed apply the exact §6.3 rule (subject public key equality, scope equal or descendant, HLC inclusively in range) with monotonic union semantics across overlapping disavows (§6.4) — classification only, never deletion or rewriting of evidence. slices.title: SPEC-6 sealed artifacts, header/payload lanes, segment manifest, HashSeq reachability, checkpoint proof, receipt pipeline, relay policy

Produce header_lane.rs: an `EnvelopeView` trait (canonical_bytes/op_id/verse_id/has_payload/verify_signature) as the seam to SPEC-1, HeaderSegmentBody scoped to one verse_id, and validation rejecting a payload-bearing record, a foreign verse_id, a bad signature, or a duplicate op_id with differing bytes while treating an identical-byte duplicate as a no-op. slices.title: SPEC-7 commit/preview wire frames, durable cursor, session generations, subscription/resume/snapshot, preview isolation
slices.brief: Implement the SPEC-7 commit and preview wire protocol as transport-agnostic types in fe-canonical-log/src/wire/, reusing wave-1 primitives (cbor encode/decode, envelope::Hash32, frontier::SortedFrontier) and adding NO axum, tower, or tokio-net dependency (tokio is available as a dev-dependency for async tests only). Read docs/spec/canonical-log/commit-preview-wire.md §1.7, §2.1 (the common frame), §2.2 (session authorization), §2.3 (the message-type registry), §3 (the durable cursor and its four required registry functions), §4.1-§4.3 (commit submit/ack/delta), §5.1 (subscribe/resume/replay), §5.2 (snapshot recovery), §6.3 (the protocol-error category table), §7.1-§7.2 (preview) and §8 (the thirteen named conformance tests). Produce frame.rs and error.rs: WIRE_VERSION = 1; a MessageType enum with the EXACT discriminants from §2.3 (Authorize=1, Authorized=2, CommitSubmit=10, CommitAck=11, CommitDelta=12, Subscribe=13, Resume=14, ReplayComplete=15, SnapshotRequired=16, SceneSnapshot=17, SnapshotAck=18, AuthorizationRevalidationRequired=19, PreviewSend=20, PreviewDelta=21, PreviewDropped=22, ProtocolError=255) with direction-check helpers; decode_frame/encode_frame over the canonical CBOR codec rejecting unsupported versions, unknown types, wrong direction, non-canonical encoding, duplicate keys and extra body keys; and ProtocolErrorCategory covering every row of the §6.3 table. Cursor validation must bind the D-CL19 sorted-frontier commitment via SortedFrontier::commitment — a tampered frontier (wrong order or wrong hash) must produce InvalidFrontierCommitment, never silent acceptance. Produce session.rs: authorize/authorized/authorization_revalidation_required bodies, a CapabilityVerifier trait (consumed, not implemented), and a SessionAuthorizationTable holding a MONOTONIC session-authorization generation, rejecting a binding-id collision that carries a different chain or principal, and exposing is_generation_valid so every other handler rejects a stale-generation frame before reaching commit/replay/snapshot/preview logic. slices.title: SPEC-4 materializer identity, admission error taxonomy, and store/verifier/materializer trait contracts
slices.brief: Implement the pure, DB-free half of SPEC-4 in fe-canonical-log/src/materialize/, reusing wave-1 primitives (envelope::Hash32, frontier::SortedFrontier for anything frontier-shaped) and defining no frontier hashing of your own. Read docs/spec/canonical-log/log-first-materialization.md §1.5 (materializer version identity), §2.1-§2.3 (the validate-then-log pipeline order), §3.1-§3.6 (exactly-once append, apply markers, atomicity, and the rebuild fallback), §4.1-§4.7 (deterministic causal replay), §5 (the error-category table), §6.1-§6.5 (rebuild and checkpoint binding) and §8 (the eleven named conformance tests). Produce identity.rs: MaterializerVersion { materializer_id: String, version: u32 } as an explicitly hand-authored value that MUST NOT be derived from CARGO_PKG_VERSION or any build identity (§1.5 requires an explicit change), ProjectionIdentity binding a materializer version to a branch id, and ApplyMarkerKey binding a projection identity to an op_id — with a test proving a version bump yields a distinct ProjectionIdentity and ApplyMarkerKey for the same branch. Produce errors.rs: AdmissionOutcome with exactly one variant per §5 row (InvalidEnvelope, UnauthorizedOperation, InvalidPayload, PreconditionFailed, MissingParent{missing}, UnknownSchema{schema_hash}, OpaquePayload{op_id}, MaterializationFailed, CheckpointMismatch) plus is_quarantine()/is_reject() implementing the §5.1/§5.2 disposition split, and AppendOutcome/AppendError where AlreadyPresent is SUCCESS not an error and HashMismatch (claimed op_id does not equal BLAKE3 of the bytes) is distinct from IntegrityConflict (same op_id, different bytes). Produce traits.rs: VerifiedEnvelopeMeta carrying exactly the post-verification facts a materializer needs (op_id, operation_kind, branch_id, schema_hash, parents, author_public_key, wall_ms, counter); ProjectionMutation as Apply{statements, bindings} or Excluded{reason} so §4.6's requirement to retain evidence of an excluded operation is representable; and async_trait traits CandidateVerifier (verify_envelope / verify_authorization / verify_payload, all returning AdmissionOutcome on failure), VerifiedLogStore (append / get_bytes / get_meta / parents_of) and CausalMaterializer (one deterministic reduce step). Produce checkpoint_binding.rs: the §6.3 five-field binding (branch_id, frontier_commitment, segment_manifest_id, materializer_version, projection_root_hash) and a validate() implementing §6.4's consumer rule — recompute the frontier commitment via SortedFrontier::commitment and compare the manifest id and materializer version against the caller's currently selected values, returning CheckpointMismatch on any difference, with an explicit doc comment that a matching Manager+ signature alone is never proof. Do NOT implement Manager+ signing, threshold policy, storage, or GC (SPEC-5/SPEC-6 own those), and do NOT define a second checkpoint claim type — the concrete signed claim belongs to the sibling branch/checkpoint slice, and binding the two happens in the serial integration wave. slices.brief: You run ALONE after waves 1-3 have landed and the orchestrator's gate has run. Your job is the wiring the parallel leaves deliberately deferred, plus repairing any API drift between sibling slices that pre-declared each other's signatures. First, implement fe-canonical-log/src/compose.rs: impl the SPEC-6 segment CheckpointView trait for the SPEC-5 SignedCheckpointClaim (mapping frontier commitment, segment manifest id, selected frontier, replay base, and Manager+ signature verification); impl the segment ScopeKeyResolver trait over fe_canonical_log::crypto::scope_key::ScopeKeyStore; impl the segment SealedArtifactStore trait over an injected byte-store closure or trait object (do NOT introduce a fe-runtime dependency — fe-runtime pulls bevy and tokio; binding to fe_runtime::blob_store::BlobStore is left to a future fe-sync/fe-database-side adapter, which you must NOT write here); impl the SPEC-4 CandidateVerifier trait over the SPEC-1 envelope codec plus capability::verify_chain plus the author_key admission entrypoints, so verify_envelope/verify_authorization/verify_payload map onto real logic and each failure maps onto the correct §5 AdmissionOutcome variant; impl the SPEC-7 wire CapabilityVerifier over capability::verify_chain; and impl the retention slice's tombstone-compaction verdict input from the concrete checkpoint verification outcome. Second, curate fe-canonical-log/src/lib.rs: replace the wave-1 placeholder declarations with the final module set (adding compose), define the crate's public re-export surface so downstream crates import stable paths, and add a `#[deny(...)]`-free but documented statement of the dependency rule (this crate depends down on fe-sdk only). Update fe-canonical-log/src/AGENTS.md with the finished module ownership map, an index of every provisional CBOR field-numbering and AAD-prefix decision recorded in the sub-AGENTS.md files (so the owner has one place to ratify from), and the trait-composition map you just wrote. Third, add the six D-CL20 bypass-counter one-liners to fe-database/src/handlers/crud.rs — a single `crate::migration::mapping_inventory::record_bypass("CreateVerse");` style call at the top of create_verse_handler, create_fractal_handler, create_petal_handler, import_gltf_handler, rename_node_handler and duplicate_node_handler (see approximately lines 22, 76, 118, 347, 1307, 1374). These must be strictly additive, must not construct an OpLogEntry, must not call commit_operation_dual_emit, must not invent a canonical payload for any of these six kinds (forbidden by migration-plan.md §4.2.5 and D-CL20), and must not change any handler's control flow, return type or error text. Fourth, add a §canon-log-materialization section to fe-database/src/AGENTS.md pointing at fe-database/src/canon_log/AGENTS.md and fe-database/src/migration/AGENTS.md, and explicitly leave the existing §log-first-commit section intact because it still accurately documents the live legacy path. Fifth, write fe-canonical-log/tests/cross_spec_integration.rs proving the compositions hold end-to-end without a database and without networking: a signed envelope from the golden-vector fixture verifying through the composed CandidateVerifier; a capability chain gating an append and being rejected after a scope-epoch bump; a checkpoint claim that verifies as a claim but yields Unresolved/HeaderReachableOnly through the segment reachability proof when a required header or decrypt authority is missing; a sealed payload round-tripping through AAD-bound seal/open and being rejected when the AAD envelope is mutated; and a wire commit_submit -> commit_ack -> commit_delta flow over the composed verifier with mock stores. Finally, repair drift: because sibling wave-2/3 slices coded against signatures pre-declared in their briefs rather than against each other's compiled code, you are authorized to make minimal signature-alignment edits in any file created by waves 1-3, but you must NOT change any behavior the specs pin, must NOT edit fe-database/src/op_log.rs, queries.rs, space_manager.rs, role_manager.rs, merge.rs, types.rs, fe-api/src/ws.rs, fe-api/src/server.rs, or fe-sync/src/**, must NOT mount /ws/canonical in any binary, must NOT flip fe-sync's IrohDocsEngineHolder::is_available(), and must NOT touch fe-ui/** or fe-terrain/** at all. Do not run cargo yourself; the orchestrator runs the final serial gate.

spec_gaps: SPEC-1-operation-envelope: 1. NFC-normalization scope is ambiguous: operation-envelope.md §2.5 states the NFC MUST specifically for 'maps with application-defined text keys... inside a schema payload', but the golden-vector conformance oracle (operation-envelope-v1.test.mjs:265-276, `assertNfc`) recursively checks NFC on every decoded string anywhere in the tree, including fixed envelope fields like author.did. The plan applies NFC validation universally in decode_canonical (G1a) to match the actual conformance oracle, which is stricter than the literal prose scope. Should be reconciled in a spec revision.

SPEC-1-operation-envelope: 2. No spec states which crate canonically owns the did:key codec used for the Author-map binding check. operation-envelope.md §3.2 requires it at the envelope layer (SPEC-1), but identity lifecycle is SPEC-2's declared domain, and fe-identity already has a working implementation (fe-identity/src/did_key.rs) with a dependency footprint (bevy, iroh, keyring, jsonwebtoken) unsuitable for a lean codec crate. The plan creates a second, minimal, byte-compatible implementation in fe-canonical-log (G1b) and flags the duplication for owner/SPEC-2 reconciliation rather than picking a side unilaterally.

SPEC-1-operation-envelope: 3. suite_id enforcement layering is unspecified. §3.5 says suite_id 'MUST be 1... never a per-operation negotiation' and separately that 65535 'MUST be rejected on production paths', but not whether that rejection happens at header decode, at AEAD-open time, or at admission. The golden-vector oracle only asserts suite_id > 0 at decode time (operation-envelope-v1.test.mjs:351) and separately exercises the 65535 fixture successfully through decode/encode/signature/op_id — so decode must NOT reject it. The plan makes decode permissive (matches the oracle) and adds an explicit `EncryptionParams::assert_production_suite()` helper (G2) for callers on production paths, but which layer is contractually required to call it is not specified anywhere and should be pinned down (likely SPEC-4's materializer or SPEC-3's key-delivery seam).

SPEC-1-operation-envelope: 4. §6.7 requires unknown operation kinds to be validated against 'a registered schema and payload rule' and quarantined if unknown, but no registry mechanism, format, or owning spec is defined anywhere in the approved set. G4 can only pass kinds 5..=65535 through structurally unvalidated; real quarantine behavior is blocked pending that registry design.

SPEC-1-operation-envelope: 5. D-CL5 requires WIT s64 exposure for the nano-unit types, but no `.wit` interface exists for canonical-log operations (fe-plugin/wit/hexon-plugin.wit is an unrelated existing plugin surface with no op-envelope hooks). G1c adds the Rust newtypes fe-sdk-side; the actual WIT wiring is deferred until a plugin-facing operation API is specified, which is out of SPEC-1's stated focus.

SPEC-1-operation-envelope: 6. §6.2 ('every listed parent MUST have the same scope.verse_id and be admitted or held in quarantine') requires knowledge of other operations' headers, i.e. a DAG store that doesn't exist in this workstream (SPEC-5's territory). G4's `validate_structural_rules` can only check the parents array's own shape (sorted/unique/hash-length), not this cross-operation invariant — flagged in-code, not silently skipped.

SPEC-2: §9.2 (owner-continuity-grant-v1) gives no CBOR field-key table, unlike §3.1 (rotation_statement) and §6.2 (disavow payload) which enumerate exact numeric keys. G2g must invent a placeholder field layout to be implementable at all; that layout is explicitly NOT wire-final and needs an owner/SPEC-3/SPEC-4 ratification pass before any cross-implementation interop is claimed for it.

SPEC-2: §4.6 references 'an authorized Manager+ resolution operation' for rotation forks that is not defined by any of the 8 approved specs. This plan can only detect and retain forks (ForkedUnresolved); resolving them is a genuine open product/protocol decision, not an implementation gap this workstream can close.

SPEC-2: §6.5's cascading revalidation of dependent authorization facts after a disavow ('capability or semantic precondition depends on a disavowed fact') presumes a materializer dependency graph that SPEC-4 has not yet specified in enough detail to implement here; G2h's admit_disavow only classifies operations as disavowed, it does not walk descendants.

SPEC-2: SPEC-2 is written against SPEC-1 types (ScopeRef/Author/Hlc/canonical CBOR primitives, an 'envelope admission' step that already ran) that this plan assumes will be produced by a SPEC-1 workstream item referenced here as G1a. This plan's exact API expectations of G1a (a ScopeRef with verse/petal/resource fields, reusable canonical-CBOR encode/decode primitives) are inferred from operation-envelope.md §3.1/§3.5, not confirmed against an actual SPEC-1 implementation contract — reconcile file paths and type names at merge time.

SPEC-2: The crate name fe-canonical-log is an assumption, not a confirmed decision: no such crate exists in the current Cargo.toml workspace members list, and the task notes 'fe-format already has canonical-JSON Ed25519 signing (manifests only — do NOT reuse for ops)', which implies a new crate is intended but does not name it. If the SPEC-1 workstream picks a different crate name, every files path in this plan needs a mechanical substitution.

SPEC-2: §6.1's rescind authority check ('strictly higher than the authority of the original disavow issuer in the parent-induced authorization view') is defined here purely in terms of fe_policy::RoleLevel ordering, since that is the only ratified authority-ordering primitive in the workspace today; the spec's phrase 'parent-induced authorization view' more precisely means capability-chain-resolved role at the causal parent, which is a SPEC-3 concept not yet implementable — G2f's validate_rescind_authority takes the resolved RoleLevel as a caller-supplied input rather than resolving it itself, and callers must not conflate that with a wall-clock 'current' role.

SPEC-3: The Rust codec crate this contract proposes (ciborium-backed canonical CBOR in G3-01) duplicates rather than reuses SPEC-1's own codec work, because no shared `fe-canonical-log`/codec crate exists yet in the workspace and this planning pass has no visibility into the SPEC-1 workstream's concrete crate/type names. The orchestrator must reconcile G3-01's Hash32/Identifier32/ScopeMap/canonical-map primitives with whatever SPEC-1's own G1 work items produce (likely a supersede-and-delete follow-up) rather than shipping two divergent canonical-CBOR implementations long-term.

SPEC-3: SPEC-3 §2.4 step 3 requires proving the root issuer is 'a current Manager+ identity for epoch_scope, as proven by issuer_authority_id in the verified authorization view' but does not specify the exact query/record shape fe-database must expose for that proof — that binding is SPEC-2's (author-key-lifecycle.md) responsibility and is not fully specified in the text I was given to plan against; G3-04 treats it as an injected `AuthorizationSnapshot.root_issuer_is_manager_plus: bool` computed by a caller that will need to consult SPEC-2's eventual API.

SPEC-3: §2.4 step 5's 'no less restrictive' rule for the three sorted-array caveats (allowed_schema_hashes, resource_allowlist, allowed_operation_kinds) is read here as strict subset containment (child ⊆ parent, including the empty set as a valid maximal narrowing). The spec does not explicitly rule out an alternate reading (e.g. requiring non-empty overlap); if that reading is wrong, G3-03's attenuation check needs a one-line semantic correction, not a redesign.

SPEC-3: §10.3.3's crypto-shredding contract says controlled wraps are removed 'where feasible' without bounding what counts as feasible (which stores, what network partitions are acceptable to miss) — G3-07 implements best-effort local-store deletion only and flags this boundary as unresolved product policy rather than inventing a stronger guarantee.

SPEC-3: §5.1.6's duplicate-bump retention rule ('retained as auditable evidence only when neither bump is in the other's parent closure') requires full DAG parent-closure computation that is out of SPEC-3's own scope (it belongs to SPEC-1's envelope/SPEC-5's branch materializer); G3-04's admission function can only enforce the local `e -> e+1` numeric rule and must accept a pre-computed closure verdict from a SPEC-4/5-owned caller once that exists.

SPEC-4: No Rust implementation of SPEC-1's canonical envelope/op_id codec exists anywhere in this workspace yet (only the JS/Node golden-vector fixture docs/spec/canonical-log/operation-envelope-v1.test.mjs). This plan therefore cannot cite a real op_id/Hash32 Rust type or a real SPEC-1 crate name/path for its depends_on edges; S4-10's conformance suite uses hand-rolled test-only envelope bytes rather than a real codec, and the true integration point (whatever crate SPEC-1's own Workstream-G plan produces) will need a follow-up reconciliation pass once that crate exists and its work-item IDs are known.
